title: Whiteboard W5: what bounds a body's evidence-ledger memory, after option 1 (#211) halved it. Outcome: RETAIN the correction of the finding doc. EXPERIMENT: option 1b in a new draft PR into #196, judged by the kill criteria. DEFER the derived on-disk index until its revival evidence exists. Gate grant growth and option 3 stay founder/governance items (W4 and the 2026-10-14 finding). The seed 'fold into #278' is not adopted: #278 keeps its own scope and its two integrator findings.
problem: On #196 f383fd26 a running body still grows 1,240 B of resident memory per retained record (one holding mission observed every minute: about 18,700 records and 23 MB a day; 1 GB in about 43 days). Option 1 of FINDING-LEDGER-APPEND-COST-2026-10-14 (payloads on disk, #211) took it from 2,624 B; it does not bound it. Heap growth by owner at f383fd26: provenance/ledger.py 354 B and provenance/digests.py 205 B per record (record skeletons, their hex hash strings, and the lookup indexes), policy/consequence_gate.py 125 B (in-memory grants), identity/machine_passport.py 43 B, events/spine.py 40 B. The whiteboard seed was to fold W5 into #278. #278 and its parent #240 bound passports, the organ queue, the egress journal and supervisor logs; neither touches provenance/ledger.py.
founder_intent_refs: #96 comment 6852550499 (whiteboard W5) and founder decision 6852618695 (agents decide reversible items after the protocol; a default-branch merge stays the founder's)
INTENT-GREG-EMBODIED-2026-09-11 (persistent work while the founder is away)
baseline: f383fd26 (#196): file-backed ledger keeps the newest 1,024 payloads and, for every older record, a slotted skeleton (seq, ts string, type, prev_hash and hash as 64-character hex strings, corrects, hash_version, offset, length, 32-byte line digest) plus by_hash (dict), by_type (array) and lazily built by_field indexes over all history. Measured 1,239.8 B RSS per record over 7,820-23,420 records (docs/evidence/ledger-memory-w5-2026-11-13/f383fd26-rss.json) and 810 B heap per record (f383fd26-heap-attribution.json).

alternatives.name: Seed: fold W5 into #278
alternatives.description: Treat #240/#278's store bounds as W5's answer.
advantages: #240 does remove the passport share (43 B/record)
disadvantages: Does not touch the evidence ledger, the largest remaining share
Would close W5 while the measured growth continues
alternatives.revival_evidence: A measurement showing #278 on #196 bounds the body's RSS per record

alternatives.name: Compact skeletons in memory (option 1b)
alternatives.description: Hold dropped-history skeletons in fixed-width arrays (32-byte binary hashes, prev_hash implied by the previous record's hash, ts as an integer, type as a small code, offset/length/digest packed) and replace the by_hash dict with a compact hash-prefix-to-position table verified against the full hash. Same trust model as today: everything stays in process memory, the running digest is unchanged in meaning.
advantages: No new tamper surface and no new dependency
Reversible; file bytes and hashes untouched
Targets the 560 B/record ledger+digests share; estimated 4-5x smaller there
disadvantages: Still linear: estimated ~700 B/record RSS overall, about 13 MB a day
More intricate code in the evidence plane's hottest file
alternatives.revival_evidence: Not rejected: this is the experiment

alternatives.name: Derived on-disk index (option 2 variant, stdlib sqlite3)
alternatives.description: Keep the hash-chained JSONL canonical; move dropped-history skeletons and lookup indexes into a derived SQLite sidecar rebuilt from the file on open.
advantages: Memory bounded to the resident window plus fixed overhead
disadvantages: New on-disk tamper surface: a deleted index row makes select() omit a record, a false negative the Gate's double-dispatch check (grant_dispatch select) must never see
Needs an integrity design for index answers, not only for payloads
Larger review; touches every ledger reader's latency
alternatives.revival_evidence: Option 1b measured and still binding before the founder's planned uptime, plus an integrity design that makes an omitted or altered index row detectable before any absence answer is used

alternatives.name: Fewer records per read-only observation (option 3)
alternatives.description: A lighter path for read-only sensors (13 records per observation today).
advantages: Cuts every per-record cost at once, the Gate's included
disadvantages: Changes what the Gate records: a governance decision
alternatives.revival_evidence: Founder ruling on read-only observation records

advantages: #211's halving already moved weeks to months
disadvantages: Persistent operation still fails on Body 1 on a measured timescale

roles.position: Persistent work while away is active N1-path intent. The seed would close W5 without touching the ledger, which is what still grows. Correct the seed, keep the destination: bounded memory, not merely smaller.
material_concerns: Gate grant growth and records-per-observation stay founder/governance items

roles.position: 1b is the smallest change with the same trust model and the largest measured share. The on-disk index is the real bound but needs an index-integrity design first; build 1b, measure, then decide on the index with numbers.
material_concerns: Keep read-API parity with an in-memory ledger
Do not touch W3's hot-path lines without the #196 integrator

roles.position: Any index that can omit a row turns the Gate's 'has this grant already been dispatched?' into a forgeable 'no'. That rules out a naive sidecar. 1b keeps the risk where it is today (process memory), so it is acceptable only with parity and running-digest tests that cover the packed form.
material_concerns: Hash-prefix collisions must fall back to full comparison
Packed fields must still feed the type-strict running digest identically

roles.position: Measured, not projected: re-run scripts/measure_body_memory.py on the experiment and record before/after on the same scenario. Rollback must be a plain revert with byte-identical files.
material_concerns: Do not add an unreviewed dependency
A slower select() on the tick path is a regression

roles.position: Nothing written may change; every count acceptance reads must stay (the #278 lesson). Fix the stale 'None is built here' line so readers are not misled. RETAIN the doc correction.
material_concerns: Evidence files are additive under a new dated path
